summary: Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Karen C. Lang and adviser K. L. Seshagiri Rao.
Robert Zimmermann (1874–1931) was an Indologist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin around 1910–1913 and held a post at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, from circa 1914 to 1930.

Robin Coningham (born 1965) is a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. He studied at King's College (1985–1994) and the University of Cambridge (PhD, ~1989–1994), holding posts at the University of Bradford (~1994–2005) and Durham University (2005).
Roderick Chisholm (1916–1999) was a philosopher who studied at Harvard University around 1938–1942. He held posts at Brown University (~1947–1987) and the University of Massachusetts Amherst.

Roderick S. Bucknell (1937–2026) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He spent his career at the University of Queensland (~1976–2002), where he served as an associate professor from around 1990 to 2002.

Roderick Whitfield (born 1937) works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986) and SOAS University of London, where he is attested as professor emeritus in 2011.

Roger R. Jackson (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Wesleyan University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, he was Associate Professor of Religion at Carleton College (~1989–2016).

Roger T. Ames (born 1947) is a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at the University of British Columbia and National Taiwan University. He held long-term posts at the University of Hawaii (~1978–2016) and Peking University (~2016).
Roland Steiner is a scholar in Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn. He held an assistant professor post at the University of Marburg (attested 2002).

Roland Wenzlhuemer (born 1976) is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Salzburg (~1996–2002). He held posts at Heidelberg University (~2008–2017) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2017).

Rolf Alfred Stein (1911–1999) was a Sinologist and Tibetologist who studied under Pelliot, Maspero, Demiéville, Chavannes, and Bacot. He held posts at INALCO (~1948–1951), EPHE (~1951–1975), and the Collège de France (1965–1981).
Rolf Scheuermann is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher, and with traditional teacher Khenpo Chodrak Tenphel.

Romila Thapar (born 1931) is an historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University and the University of London under A. L. Basham. She held posts at the University of Delhi and Jawaharlal Nehru University.
Ron Garry is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and teacher Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer (1932–2017) worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a Tibetologist and sociologist who held posts as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong, both attested in 1998.

Ronald E. Purser (born 1956) works in religious studies, philosophy, and management. He studied under Koshin Ogui in 1985 and held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1989–1995) and San Francisco State University (~1995).

Ronald Egan (born 1948) is a Sinologist who earned his PhD from Harvard University (~1971–1977). He held posts at Harvard (~1977–1986), Wellesley College, UC Santa Barbara (~1994–2012), and Stanford University (~2012).

Ronald M. Davidson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (until 1985), and held an attested post at Fairfield University from 2002 to 2005.

Ronald Neufeldt (born 1941) is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He held a post as Associate Professor in the Religious Studies Department at the University of Calgary from circa 1977 to 2006.
